paper.title: Asymptotically-Optimal Gaussian Bandits with Side Observations

settings.name_in_paper: Gaussian bandits with general side information matrix
unmapped: Feedback is a weighted (noisy) side-observation structure: playing arm i reveals a Gaussian sample of every arm j with standard deviation sigma_{i,j} given by an arbitrary known K x K matrix Sigma (sigma_{i,j}=infinity means no information); generalizes graph feedback
The learner knows the side-information matrix Sigma
settings.definition_quote: By playing an action $i \in [K]$ the player observes a noisy sample $X_{j}$ from the reward of each arm $j \in [K]$, distributed independently as $X_j \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu_j,\sigma_{i,j}^2)$, and collects the realized value $X_i \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu_i,\sigma_{i,i}^2)$.

algorithms.name: Asymptotically-Optimal Algorithm for Gaussian Bandits with Side Observations (Algorithm 1)

symbols.c_star_i: optimal solution of the LP min sum_i c_i Delta_i s.t. sum_j c_j/sigma_{j,i}^2 >= 2/Delta_i^2 for suboptimal i and >= 2/Delta_min^2 for the optimal arm

conditions: policy is consistent: R_T/T^p -> 0 for every p>0 on every environment

source.label: thm:lower_bound
source.quote: For any environment $(\mu, \Feedback)$, the regret of any consistent policy within $T$ rounds satisfies \liminf_{T\rightarrow \infty}{\frac{R_T(\mu)}{\log{T}}} \geq \sum_{i\in [K]} c_i^*(\mu) \D_i(\mu).

results.notes: Regret defined as T mu* - E[sum X_{i_t,t}], i.e. pseudo-regret.

symbols.gamma_alg: algorithm parameter gamma in (0,1) of beta(x)=x^gamma/(2 sigma_bar^2)
symbols.c_eps_i: worst-case epsilon-approximate LP solution c*_i(mu, eps) = sup over ||mu'-mu||_inf <= eps of c*_i(mu')

source.label: thm:regret_upper_bound
source.quote: For any $\alpha>4$, $\gamma \in (0,1)$, and $\epsilon>0$, the regret of algorithm \cref{algorithm1} satisfies R_T(\mu) \leq \left(2K + \frac{8K}{\alpha-4}  + 2\right)\D_{\max} + 2\D_{\max} K \sum_{\tau\in[T]} \exp\left(-\frac{\tau^{\gamma} \epsilon^2}{4K\sm^2}\right) + \D_{\max} \left(4\alpha \sum_{j\in[K]} c^*_j(\mu,\epsilon)  \log{T}  +K \right)^{\gamma} + 4\alpha \sum_{j\in[K]} \D_j(\mu) c^*_j(\mu,\epsilon)  \log{T}.

results.notes: Algorithm solves an LP each exploration round (polynomial). Anytime: algorithm does not take T. The proof's final line differs slightly from the statement; recorded as stated in theorem.

symbols.c_eps_i: worst-case epsilon-approximate LP solution c*_i(mu, eps)

source.label: cor:asymptotic_optimality
source.quote: As the time horizon tends to infinity, the regret of \cref{algorithm1} satisfies \limsup_{T\rightarrow\infty} \frac{R_T(\mu)}{\log{T}} \leq 4\alpha \sum_{j\in[K]} \D_j(\mu) c^*_j(\mu,\epsilon).

results.notes: Matches the lower bound up to constant factor 4*alpha as epsilon -> 0.
